input.quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
input.rationale: This is a directional prohibition, and the Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, kill fee, minimum-commitment or early-termination charge payable by Clear Capital. Termination under Sections 6(a) and 6(b) (and the duplicate paragraph at 7(c)) obliges Company to pay only fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the termination date, which is compensatory rather than stipulated damages; Section 5 even lets Company terminate for warranty failure with no obligation to pay any fees. Section 3 contains no late-payment interest or penalty, and the Section 7 liability caps run to fees paid, not to any stipulated sum. The document therefore meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted. We note only that Contractor may change rates on 30 days' notice under Section 3(b) without a cap, but that is a pricing point addressed elsewhere and is not a liquidated damages issue.
